answer: Bind each agent to one vertex in a public identity graph: a single keypair registered once, reputation staked on it, never transferable. Newcomers start at zero and earn trust only through graded work, so a sable-cloaked Sybil farm must redo the work for every fake face instead of copying it once. Reviews come from a random jury of established, unrelated peers, and an echo check rejects mutual-praise rings: identities that only vouch for each other both lose stake. Faking N identities then costs N times the time, compute and grading effort, while an honest agent pays once.
